title: 一日の目標は六十本だ  (The Daily Goal Is Sixty)

segments.t: Seeing a stack of unsold cassette tapes, our protagonist's salesman instincts suddenly wake up. He marches into a specialty shop, charms the owner into buying twenty tapes for sixty thousand yen cash, and proposes an ambitious partnership on the street outside. Listen to him work his magic.
俺がこれを売るよ。
そう簡単に売れないよ。
あんた、面白いね。買ってやるよ。
ありがとうございます。さすがオーナー様、お目が高い！
売れた！一本三千円で六万円だ。
あんた営業マンだったのかよ？
そうだ。これ、一日何本ぐらい売れてるんだ？
まあ、多くて一日二本だな。
じゃあ他の店も行こう。一日の目標は六十本だ。
ちょっと待てよ。俺と組むってことか？
だめか？
あんた、この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
Notice how the protagonist switches smoothly between silky customer flattery inside the shop and brisk business numbers outside.
そう簡単に売れないよ。
'They will not sell that easily.'  Check out
簡単に
this word means easily or simply, and
売れない
comes from the verb for selling well on the market—distinct from what the seller does.
買ってやるよ。
"'I will buy them from you.' Amused by the pitch, the shopkeeper uses " Check out
買ってやるよ
, doing the newcomer a favour.
さすがオーナー様、お目が高い！
"'As expected of you, Owner, you have a keen eye!' Every salesperson in Japan knows " It features
さすが
, 'true to your reputation!', and the classic flattery
お目が高い
—literally 'your eyes are high', meaning refined taste!
売れた！一本三千円で六万円だ。
"'They sold! At three thousand yen apiece, that is sixty thousand yen.' Long cylindrical or spooled items like tapes, bottles, and umbrellas count with the counter for long things: " Check out
一本三千円
totals
六万円
, sixty thousand yen.
あんた営業マンだったのかよ？
'Wait, were you a salesman?'  They are saying
営業マン
blends the Japanese word for sales with the English word 'man'—the everyday word for a sales rep.
そうだ。これ、一日何本ぐらい売れてるんだ？
"'Roughly how many of these sell per day?' Asking " Check out
何本ぐらい
combines the word for how many tapes with the word for approximately.
まあ、多くて一日二本だな。
'Well, two a day at most.'  It features
多くて
comes from the word for many, and at the start of an estimate it this word means 'at the very most'.
じゃあ他の店も行こう。
"It means 'Then let us hit other shops too.' " In this sentence,
他の店
this word means other shops, and
行こう
this word is the energetic 'let us go!' form of the verb to go.
一日の目標は六十本だ。
"'Our daily target is sixty.' Where the young hustler sells two, our protagonist calmly sets " Notice how
目標
, target or goal, at
六十本
, sixty tapes!
ちょっと待てよ。
'Hold on a second.'  Starting off with
ちょっと待てよ
turns the verb to wait into 'hey, wait a minute!'
あんた、この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
'Do you really have the resolve to step into this world?'  Focus on
覚悟
this word means mental readiness to face consequences—'are you truly prepared for what comes next?' Now let's listen to this sixty-thousand-yen triumph again.
俺がこれを売るよ。
そう簡単に売れないよ。
あんた、面白いね。買ってやるよ。
ありがとうございます。さすがオーナー様、お目が高い！
売れた！一本三千円で六万円だ。
あんた営業マンだったのかよ？
そうだ。これ、一日何本ぐらい売れてるんだ？
まあ、多くて一日二本だな。
じゃあ他の店も行こう。一日の目標は六十本だ。
ちょっと待てよ。俺と組むってことか？
だめか？
あんた、この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
Remember the expression for easily, the phrase for complimenting someone's good taste, the word for a goal, and the command to say hold on! One final scene concludes Episode One.
また会いましょう。
